previousPlan.title: Recall the responses, then let them flow
previousPlan.goal: Recall “I’m well,” “And you?” and “I’m tired” independently, then use them in the full conversation.
previousPlan.recap: First ask for “I’m well,” “And you?” and “I’m tired” separately, one at a time, with no Portuguese model. Record whether each response was independent, prompted or corrected. Then briefly retrieve Oi, Bom dia, Eu sou Dan and the meaning/production of Como você está?.
previousPlan.warmup: Listen to the first attempts before correcting. Recheck cansado if needed; it improved quickly last lesson. Estou bem was clear after modeling, so prioritise retrieval over unnecessary sound repetition. Eu sou Dan and Como você está? were clear and independently recalled on 11 September.
previousPlan.newMaterial: Consolidate the three existing responses first. Only if all are independently recalled from meaning cues, introduce one new Estou… response such as Estou animado (“I’m excited”). Otherwise keep new material at zero. Estou animado remains Planned until actually taught.
previousPlan.roleplay: Run the full opening and response exchange without supplying answers: Oi, bom dia. Eu sou Dan. Como você está? Reply with Estou bem, e você? or Estou cansado as appropriate. Alternate roles, repeat the exchange, then recheck individual responses outside the memorized sequence.
previousPlan.adapt: A smooth memorized sequence does not establish isolated recall. If a response needs a model, briefly review it and test it later from a meaning cue. Keep Estou bem, E você? and Estou cansado Developing until independent retrieval is demonstrated. Do not award mastery for repetition.
previousPlan.close: End with a spoken recap and dated lesson log. Record material practised, independent versus prompted recall, errors, pronunciation, comprehension, role-play result and next priority. Mark new material as taught only if it was actually introduced.
previousPlan.notes: Prepared from Dan’s supplied 11 September 2026 lesson log. This next lesson is proposed and has not been completed. The previous lesson consolidated existing material; no new phrases were marked mastered.

Take a moment. Then say it when you’re ready.

transcript.speaker: Tutor
transcript.text:
Great job, Dan—that was clear.

Next one: how do you say “And you?” in Portuguese?

Pause and try to recall it before you say anything.

transcript.speaker: Tutor

It’s “E você?” 

Say it slowly once if you want, then we’ll test recall again soon.

next.goal: Recall E você? independently from the separate English meaning cue “And you?”, then recheck Estou bem from “I’m well.” Do not introduce new material until both are securely recalled.
next.recap: Ask for “I’m well” and “And you?” one at a time, with no Portuguese model. Record each as independent, prompted, repeated or uncertain. Do not count repetition as mastery.
next.warmup: Begin with the English cue “And you?” and wait for independent recall. Then use “I’m well” as a separate cue. Avoid supplying the Portuguese phrase before the attempt.
